new: Doubtful construction. bhāryā-vyañjanāḥ is read as an accusative plural feminine object (female agents in the guise of wives), following the glossary rendering of X-vyañjanā. pareṣām is read with bhāryā-vyañjanāḥ ("wives of others"); alternative: pareṣām māṇavaiḥ = "with the young men of others", or bhāryā-vyañjanāḥ as nominative (the female agents themselves cause the young men to rejoice). Reviewer: pareṣām cannot grammatically qualify the first member of the compound bhāryā-vyañjanāḥ; the adjacent reading 'with the young men of others' (pareṣām māṇavaiḥ), or bhāryā-vyañjanāḥ as nominative subject, is at least as natural as the draft. Rendering left literal; a person should decide.
why: reviewer (minor): A genitive cannot attach to the first member of the compound, so 'wives of others' (Hindi दूसरों की पत्नियों के वेश) joins pareṣām to the compound against the grammar; the adjacent reading pareṣām māṇavaiḥ ('with the young men of others') is at least as natural. Left as drafted because the sense is unclear.
reviewer (minor): Gender: the compound ends in neuter ādhāna, so n., not m.
